remote.description: Whether it may see and use other machines.

Account.description:
What the API is allowed to see: no secret, and no hash of one either.

Named `Account` because that is the schema name in `openapi/openapi.json`.

email.description: Address of the login, once a usage verification has read one.

envKeys.description:
The variable names an env account sets, in the order they were typed.

Names only: the list a picker, a session row and this page all read has
no value in it. The block itself is returned only by
`GET /api/accounts/{id}/env`, which the settings page calls when it
opens an env account for editing — an explicit read, not one every list
response carries.

id.description: Stable uuid; also the name of the account's data directory.

label.description: Display name the user gave it.

rest.description:
The limits this instance has seen the account hit that have not lifted
yet: one entry per scope, active ones only.

Recorded, not acted on — nothing switches accounts or holds a queue
because of it. Empty when the account is not
resting; per instance, because the log it comes from is.

rotation.description:
Whether the account is in its CLI's rotation pool: a session whose
account hits a limit may be moved onto it and carry on there.

Defaults to `true` for a Claude OAuth account and `false` for an env or
Codex account.

unverified.description:
Why the credential was stored without being checked.

Only ever set on the reply that stored it, and only when the live check
could not run at all — no `claude` on `PATH`, a timeout, a rate limit. It
is not persisted and never appears in `GET /api/accounts`: it exists so
the client can say "saved, but nobody has proved this works" instead of
implying a check that did not happen.

usageEnabled.description: Whether the quota panel probes this account.

AccountConflict.description: The `409` body when a token is already stored.

existingLabel.description: The label the token is already filed under.

env.description:
The `KEY=VALUE` block, for `kind: env`. Returned only by
`GET /api/accounts/{id}/env`.

provider.description: Which CLI it is for; defaults to claude.

rotation.description: Whether it joins the rotation pool; defaults by provider and kind.

secret.description: The OAuth token, for `kind: oauth_token`. Never returned.

accountId.description:
The account new sessions follow; `null` chooses the local login, which
then stays where they start even while it is signed out.

automatic.description:
`true` (with `accountId: null`) clears the default rather than choosing
the local login: new sessions then start on the local login, or — while
it is signed out — on an account in the auto-rotation pool standing in
for it (`GET /api/accounts/start`). What a fresh install has.

provider.description: Which CLI's default to set; defaults to claude.

env.description:
The account's whole block, one `KEY=VALUE` per line, as the editor
shows it. Values included: this route exists to read them back.

AccountFrom.description: Where a request's `accountId` came from, when it was not somebody's pick.

AccountLimitEvent.description: One entry in the limit log.

accountId.description: The account it happened under; `null` for the machine's own login.

id.description: Increasing; newer events have larger ids.

model.description: The model the session was running, when known.

raw.description: What the CLI said, redacted and cut to 500 characters.

scope.description: `all`, or the model family a weekly window belongs to.

source.description:
Which hook saw it: `claude:result`, `claude:rate_limit_event`,
`claude:exit`, `codex:turn` or `codex:rate_limits`. The part before the
colon is the CLI.

untilAt.description: When the limit lifts, ISO-8601, if anything said or a default applied.

AccountList.description: `GET /api/accounts` and everything that returns the whole list.

defaultAccountId.description:
Account new claude sessions follow; `null` is none: the local login, or,
while it is signed out and nobody chose it (`local.claude.isDefault`), an
account in the pool standing in for it (`GET /api/accounts/start`).

defaultCodexAccountId.description: Account new codex sessions follow; `null` is none, as for claude.

local.description:
The machine's own login for each CLI — the one a session with no account
runs on — and whether it can start a session right now. A picker uses it
to stop offering a signed-out local login as the default.

AccountProvider.description: Which CLI an account's credential is for.

AccountQuota.description: One stored account's live window usage, read off its sessions or probed with its own usage login.

email.description: Address of the login, when one is known.

error.description: Absent when fine or still probing.

id.description: The account's uuid.

source.description: Where the newest window was read; absent when there are no windows.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 of the last reading that produced windows.

usageEnabled.description: Whether the quota panel probes it.

AccountRef.description: The account a session runs under, as the session payloads name it.

id.description: The account's uuid.

AccountRest.description: One account resting, as `Account.rest` reports it.

class.description: Which kind of limit put it here.

observedAt.description: When the limit was seen, ISO-8601.

reason.description: The line of the CLI's output that said why, redacted.

scope.description: `all`, or the model family a weekly window belongs to.

sessionId.description: The session it was seen in.

source.description:
Which hook saw it: `claude:result`, `claude:rate_limit_event`,
`claude:exit`, `codex:turn` or `codex:rate_limits`. The part before the
colon is the CLI.

untilAt.description:
When the rest ends, ISO-8601; `null` until it is cleared or the
credential changes.

AccountStart.description: `GET /api/accounts/start`: the login a start that names no account runs on.

accountId.description: The stored account; `null` is the machine's own login.

model.description:
The model to send, when the start lets this answer choose it
(`chooseModel`) and the choice decides where it runs: one of this
login's own models that the rule places on this login. `null` when the
start names its model, or when any model lands on the same login — a
composer then takes the head of the login's list, as it always has.

placed.description:
Whether a start that names no account, sent with `model` (or with the
model the query named), lands on `accountId` by this same rule. `false`
only when no login's own models land on it: a start that wants this pair
then has to name the account.

env.description:
A replacement `KEY=VALUE` block, for an env account.

Replaces the whole block: what is not in the text is not set. Checked
before it is stored, exactly as a replacement token is.

rotation.description: Put the account in or take it out of the rotation pool.

secret.description:
A replacement credential — re-authorization by paste.

Checked against Anthropic before it is stored, and never returned. The
account keeps its id, so every session bound to it carries on under it.

description.description: What the Task call asked for.

items.description: The items, head and tail of an over-long transcript.

omittedItems.description: How many were dropped out of the middle.

totalItems.description: How many items the transcript holds in total.

AggregatorCopy.description:
What this computer holds of one device's copy (S1-5): counts and times,
never content.

indexAsOfMs.description: When its agent last listed them (ms).

indexRows.description: Sessions in its index, as copied (`null`: no index yet).

online.description: Whether it is online now (`null`: not known).

statusAtMs.description: When its agent last signed its status (ms).

AggregatorHost.description:
One device that runs AI and accepts this computer's control, and the
content keys (its machine-key epochs) held of it here.

copy.description:
What is copied of it here (S1-5); `null` before anything is, and for
a caller who may not see other devices (§4.6: only whoever manages the
link, or a local account the owner let see them).

id.description: Its id.

policy.description:
Whether its agent declared `policy/1` (refuses this computer its admin
routes); `null` until the hub said.

enabled.description:
`false` turns it off and deletes the other devices' keys here; `true`
turns it on again (chain v3 needs nothing from droppen.app for it: this
computer controls with the identity it already has).

additionalProperties.description: One label or free text, or every label chosen for a multi-select question.

answers.description:
The exact question text, as asked → its answer. May be empty when
`response` says it all.

notes.description: The exact question text → a note beside the choice.

response.description: Free text, with the choices or instead of them.

ApiChat.description:
A whole API-backed chat, exactly as it is stored.

`#[serde(default)]` keeps a hand-edited or half-written file readable: the
TypeScript casts the parsed JSON to `ApiChat` and checks only `id` and
`messages`, so a file missing `title` degrades rather than disappearing.

id.description: Stable uuid; also the file name.

model.description: The model this chat is answered by.

title.description: Display name, seeded from the first message.

ApiChatMessage.description:
One turn of an API-backed chat.

Every field defaults, for the same reason [`ApiChat`]'s do: the TypeScript
validated nothing below `id` and `messages`, so a turn missing its timestamp
still has to read.

type.description: Which kind of app to start.

AppInfo.description: One running app, as the API describes it.

id.description: Opaque id; also the `/embed/{id}/` path segment.

type.description: Which kind of app this is.

apps.description: Every instance whose process is still running.

AppType.description: The kinds of app that can be started.

Attachment.description: A file parked in the uploads directory, ready to attach to a message.

isImage.description: Whether the composer should draw a thumbnail for it.

name.description: The original filename, preserved so the download name means something.

AuthSession.description: One live login, as the account panel lists it.

current.description: Whether this is the session making the request.

id.description:
Its id, which is `sha256(token)` — the same value the server stores.
Knowing it is not knowing the token, and cannot be turned into one.

label.description: What the client called itself when it logged in, or `null`.

lastSeenAt.description: Last time it was used, ISO-8601, to within five minutes.

sessions.description: The caller's own live sessions, oldest first.

AuthStatus.description:
What `GET /api/auth/status` answers, logged in or not.

Answered to anyone, so it says nothing but these few things — all of which
are either about the caller or visible from the way every other route
answers them anyway.

authOff.description:
Whether authentication is switched off (`auth.enabled = false`), so
that every route answers anyone who can reach the port.

authRequired.description:
Whether a caller has to sign in: `true` unless authentication is
switched off. Nobody is let in for where they connect from.

desktopApp.description:
Whether the Droppen desktop app runs this server and owns its login
(`crate::desktop_app`): the web app then shows no password change, no
sign-out and no sign-in to Droppen through a browser popup.

droppenEnv.description:
What those commands need in their environment to act on this server's
instance, to put before `droppenPath` (`APP_INSTANCE=bob …/droppen
setup-code`): the instance when it is not `default`, and where this
server keeps its files when that is not the usual place
(`crate::program::droppen_env`). Empty for the usual install; values
not yet quoted for a shell. Servers older than this field send none.

droppenPath.description:
How a person on this device runs this server's binary, for the commands
the web app asks them to type (`<droppenPath> user add <name>`): the
`droppen` link beside the running binary if there is one, else the
binary itself, with the home directory as `~` (`crate::program`). A
path, not yet quoted for a shell. Servers older than this field send
none; the web app then says `remote-hand-server`.

setupRequired.description:
Whether this device has no user account yet (the desktop app's own
account does not count). A caller with no session then gets the setup
page: open the page from the device (`remote-hand-server open`, or the
app), or make the first account with the one-time setup code.

user.description:
Who the request's token says it is, or `null`: an account name,
`local:owner` for a session opened with a local-open token, or
`cloud:<device>` for a device bridged in through Droppen.

BackgroundTask.description:
One piece of work claude started and left running behind its turn.

The stream says far more about these than a count can carry: every
`system:task_started` names the task and says what kind it is, and every
`system:background_tasks_changed` republishes the whole live list with the
same fields. Keeping only the count meant a session could say "3 background
tasks" and nothing else — not what they are, not when they began — while the
CLI had been describing each of them all along.

Everything but the id is optional because the CLI's own shape is: a snapshot
entry may carry a `task_type` and no `description`, and this parses
tolerantly rather than dropping a task it cannot fully describe.

description.description: What claude said the task is doing, when it said anything.

durationMs.description:
How long it has been running, in milliseconds, by the CLI's clock.

The CLI's own duration rather than `startedAt` arithmetic, which is wrong
by however long this server was down or attached late.

id.description: The CLI's own `task_id`, stable for the task's life.

lastToolName.description: The tool the task was last seen using — `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`.

startedAt.description:
When this server first heard of the task, by its own clock.

Not the CLI's start time, which the stream does not carry: after a
restart the whole list is reconstructed from one snapshot, and every task
in it is first seen then. Honest about what it is — the moment remote-hand
learned of the task — rather than precise about something it cannot know.

subagentType.description:
Which agent type is running it, for a `local_agent` task.

The five fields below all come from `system:task_progress`, which the CLI
republishes every few seconds for every live task and which this server
used to step over: a background panel could say "Scout the codebase" and
a stopwatch, while the stream had been reporting the tool it was in, its
token spend and its tool count the whole time. Absent — rather than
null — until the first progress line for that task arrives, so a client
can tell "no progress yet" from "progress said nothing".

taskType.description:
The CLI's `task_type` — `local_agent`, `local_bash`, whatever it adds
next. Passed through rather than parsed into an enum, because a value
this server has never heard of is still worth showing.

toolUseId.description:
The id of the `tool_use` that launched it, when the CLI said which.

The join key between this list and the transcript. A client holding both
can only pair them by this: the transcript knows what the child was
handed — the prompt, the command — and this knows whether it is *still
running*, which the transcript cannot say for a child that reports
through its own channel. Without the pairing a client has to choose one
source and be wrong the other way.

Null for a task this server only ever heard about in a
`background_tasks_changed` snapshot, which carries no `tool_use_id` —
most often after a restart, when the whole list is reconstructed from
one. Such a task is still worth listing; it just cannot be joined.

toolUses.description: How many tools it has run so far.

totalTokens.description: Tokens the task has spent so far, as the CLI counts them.

ChatKind.description:
Which backend a chat runs on.

One enum for all three of the contract's `"claude" | "codex" | "api"` fields
— `ChatNew.backend`, `ChatSummary.kind` and `ChatNewResult.kind` — because
they are the same three values and always agree.

chats.description: Every chat from both backends, newest first.

models.description: Model ids the provider offers, sorted.

accountFrom.description:
`"start"`: `accountId` is the account `GET /api/accounts/start` named
for a pair no model-less start reaches (`placed: false`), not a pick —
logged as the start rule's choice and checked again at the spawn.

accountId.description:
Run a CLI chat under a stored account of its CLI; `null` means the local
login. Absent follows the CLI's default — and, with none, skips a local
login known to be signed out (see `accounts::rotation::start_for`).

effort.description: Reasoning effort, for the CLI backends.

text.description:
The first message. Required for the CLI backends, because spawning the
CLI *is* the first send; ignored by the API backend, which is created
empty and sent to afterwards.

id.description:
The new chat's id. Nullable in the contract because codex generates its
own thread id, so there is a shape for "started, id not known yet".

kind.description: The backend the chat ended up on.

ChatProviderInfo.description:
What a client is allowed to learn about the provider.

Named `ChatProviderInfo` because that is the schema name in
`openapi/openapi.json`.

hasKey.description: Whether a key is stored. The key itself is never sent.

ChatProviderUpdate.description: The body of `PUT /api/chat-provider`; every field is a patch.

apiKey.description: New key; an explicit empty string clears the stored one.

baseUrl.description: New endpoint root; absent leaves it alone.

model.description: New default model; absent leaves it alone.

ChatRole.description:
Who said something.

Spelled `ChatRole` rather than `Role` because `Schematic::name()` is the
Rust identifier and the schema registry has one component per name: a second
`Role` would silently merge with [`crate::sessions::util::Role`], whose
values are `user | assistant | system`. The contract inlines this enum, so
the component name itself is free.

ChatSummary.description: One row of the chat list.

id.description: The chat id — a session id for CLI chats, a uuid for API ones.

model.description:
The model, for API chats. CLI chats are answered by whatever the CLI is
configured with, which remote-hand does not know, so it is `null`.

items.description: The tasks, in the order the CLI numbered them.

ChecklistItem.description: One task in a session's checklist.

id.description: The task's own id, as the CLI numbered it.

status.description:
Where it got to: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`. Carried as free
text rather than an enum because the vocabulary is the CLI's own — a word
this server has not seen should reach the UI, not fail the request.

title.description: What the task is; the sidecar calls this field `subject`.

source.description: Where the newest window was read; absent when there are no windows.

ClaudeRoot.description:
Which Claude config root a session file lives in.

The name is the OpenAPI component name in `openapi/openapi.json`
(`ClaudeRoot`), so `Schematic::name()` and the golden contract agree.

CliChoice.description: The model/effort a session actually ran with, per its own transcript.

at.description: Timestamp of the transcript entry the reading came from.

CloudAccount.description: This computer's Droppen account, as far as it knows it.

email.description: The account's e-mail address, as the droppen.app popup said it (display only).

fingerprint.description: The account key's fingerprint, as `agent enroll` shows it.

id.description: The account id (`a-…`).

CloudAggregator.description:
The aggregator: this computer controlling the account's other devices
with its one identity (local-aggregator §5, S1-4).

askedMs.description: When it last asked the account's admins for keys it lacks.

hosts.description: The devices that accept this computer's control, and the keys held of each.

signedIn.description: Signed in to the hub as a device now.

state.description:
`on` (it runs: the link runs and the chain names this computer),
`off`, or `pending` (a key an older release prepared for a sign-in).

handoffUrl.description:
The droppen.app address that answers it through the browser (§4.9),
for the caller who opened it only (it carries the attempt's state).

id.description: Its id.

mine.description: Whether the caller opened it (only they can finish it).

CloudHandoff.description:
How the caller's last browser hand-off ended (§4.9): droppen.app's reply
came back through `/link/return`.

error.description: Why it failed: the error code (`hub_unreachable`, `refused`, …).

machine.description: The machine id the hub assigned.

outcome.description:
`receiving` (taken: enrolling now), `handed_over` (the hub took the
enrollment: a device of the account completes it) or `failed`.

changes.description: Account changes this machine saw (newest last).

connected.description: Signed in to the hub now.

devices.description: Current devices and machines in the account.

refused.description:
The hub refuses this computer's sign-in: retried, and never taken as
a removal (only the verified chain removes it).

removedMs.description: When this machine learnt it was removed.

running.description: The link runs in this server.

sinceMs.description: Since when (ms) it has been connected, or not.

CloudMachine.description: This computer as a machine of the account.

fingerprint.description:
Its keys' fingerprint: 8 groups of 4 hex digits, the same string the
droppen.app consent page shows.

id.description: Its id in the account (`m-…`), once the hub assigned one.

CloudRotation.description:
Renewing this computer's identity key (`docs/host-identity-rotation.md`
§3.5, §3.7): what the local settings show.

code.description:
For a renewal confirmed on this computer: the code to type on the
admin device (`XXXX-XXXX`), for ten minutes.

codeExpiresMs.description: Until when (ms) the code is shown.

previousFingerprint.description: Its fingerprint before (8 groups of 4 hex digits).

renewedMs.description: When (ms) it took the renewed key.

state.description:
`idle`; `staged` (a new key waits for the renewal to be written);
`renewed` (it took a renewed key within the last day); `refused` (the
hub refuses its key as renewed but showed no renewal: it retries,
nothing else changes); `foreign` (its identity key was replaced
elsewhere — its own chain gives its id keys it does not hold, for
example after restoring a backup made before a renewal: the link
stopped; `POST /api/cloud/re-enroll-fresh` adds it again under a new
identity); `unreadable` (renewed, and a staged key it may have been
renewed to does not read: the link stopped until the file beside its
key is put right — never taken for `foreign`).

CloudStatus.description: `GET /api/cloud`: where this computer stands with Droppen. Nothing secret.

accounts.description:
Every local account and whether it sees the other devices here — for
whoever manages the link only (empty for anyone else).

canClaim.description:
Nobody owns this device's link (it was enrolled from the command line,
or its owner's local account is gone), so nobody sees the other
devices here; the caller manages the link and may claim it
(`POST /api/cloud/claim`).

canManage.description: Whether the caller may manage the link.

handoff.description:
How the caller's last browser hand-off ended (kept for as long as an
attempt lives).

hub.description: The hub, as the agent signs in to it (`wss://…`).

hubWeb.description:
Where a browser signs in to the hub, which the sign-in popup and the
browser hand-off open: the app origin the hub's
`/.well-known/droppen-hub` names (`https://my.droppen.app`), else the
hub's own origin as `https://`.

link.description: The hub connection, once there is a state.

localAuth.description: Whether local authentication is on (signing in needs it).

owner.description: The local account that signed this computer in.

remoteAccess.description: Which local accounts may see other machines.

state.description:
`none` (never signed in), `enrolling` (waiting for a device to add
it), `linked`, `not_hosting` (still in the account, but not running
AI in it: no streams, no channels, until a device makes it run AI
again), `removed` (the account removed it) or `broken` (its state
does not load).

blocked.description:
Whether ordinary usage is blocked right now — the account is out, and
the next message will be refused rather than merely expensive.

`null` is *unknown*, not "fine": only the app server is asked this, so
the log fallback always leaves it null rather than implying an account
with 0% left is still able to run.

source.description: Which of the two readings above this is.

updatedAt.description:
ISO-8601 of the reading. For [`CodexQuotaSource::AppServer`] this is the
moment the app server answered; for the log fallback it is the timestamp
the rollout entry carried, which may be hours old.

CodexQuotaSource.description:
Where a Codex reading came from.

On the wire, for the same reason [`crate::models::ModelListSource`] is: the
app server answers with the account's live numbers, while the session logs
only say what some past turn was told. One shown as the other is how a panel
tells a user they have 30% left of a week they have already spent.

CommandEnv.description: One environment variable of a command the web app shows.

CommandTool.description: What a command is for: one of the two CLIs, or git.

ComposerChoice.description: One remembered set of composer choices.

model.description: Model id, as the CLI's `--model` takes it.

updatedAt.description: When this entry was last written, ISO-8601.

defaults.description: Per-source fallback used for new sessions and sessions without an entry.

sessions.description: Keyed `source/sessionId`; oldest entries beyond the cap are dropped.

id.description: The new session's id. The session it was copied from keeps its own.

source.description: Which CLI it belongs to; always `claude`.

DayUsage.description: One calendar day of the window.

cacheRead.description: Tokens served from the prompt cache.

cacheWrite.description: Tokens written into the prompt cache.

DiagramStyle.description: How a Mermaid diagram in a message renders.

DroppenAccounts.description: The Droppen accounts stored for one CLI.

defaultLabel.description: The label of the one new sessions follow, if one is the default.

total.description: How many. Each was verified when it was saved.

Error.description:
The error body every failing route returns.

Named `Error` because that is the schema name in `openapi/openapi.json` —
`Schematic::name()` is the Rust identifier, so the two have to agree.

FileRef.description: A file the item points at, offered to the UI as a download chip.

name.description: Base name, shown on the chip.

FileUpload.description:
Everything gotcha cannot express about those routes.
The `multipart/form-data` body both upload routes read.

gotcha derives nothing from a `Multipart` extractor — the generated
`requestBody` names the media type and stops — so the one part the handlers
actually read is documented explicitly, matching `z.object({ file: z.any() })`
in the golden contract.

file.description: The file part; the only one either route looks at.

email.description: The account's e-mail address, as the popup said it (display only).

FinishResult.description: The enrollment the hub took (202: a device completes it).

machine.description: The machine id the hub assigned.

FirstAgent.description:
The tool step 03 picked: [`super::ToolId`]'s two values, as a type of its own.
A `Nullable` enum is nullable wherever the schema names it
(`openapi_ext::hoist_nullable_refs`), and `ToolId` must stay non-null for
the tools report.

FirstProgress.description:
What step 03 chose for the first session. Nothing is started from it: the
guide's Finish opens the empty-session view with it filled in.

prompt.description: The first message, in the words the user saw.

FirstUnread.description: Where the messages a visit has not read yet begin.

count.description:
How many agent messages are newer than `after`, which is what the
client's button says. Not capped at 99 like `unreadCount`: this walks the
whole transcript. Zero exactly when `index` is `null`.

index.description:
Absolute index of the first agent message newer than `after`, in the
feed's own item numbering — the one the history route pages by and a
transcript row's `data-ti` carries — or `null` when there is none.

FolderTool.description: Who ran sessions in a folder.

FontSize.description: UI scale, applied as the document root font size.

FsEntry.description: One row of a directory listing.

mtime.description: Modification time, ISO-8601; filled on the same terms as `sizeBytes`.

name.description: The entry's own name, not a path.

sizeBytes.description: Size in bytes; only regular files carry one, and it is null when the stat failed.

entries.description: Directories first, then names in ascending order.

parent.description: The parent directory, or null at the home directory — the browser's ceiling.

path.description: The resolved absolute path that was listed.

FsRead.description: A file's text, up to the read cap.

binary.description: True when the slice held a NUL byte, in which case `content` is empty.

content.description: The decoded slice, or an empty string for a binary file.

path.description: The resolved absolute path that was read.

sizeBytes.description: The file's full size, which may exceed the returned slice.

truncated.description: True when the file is larger than the 256 KiB read cap.

path.description: Absolute path of the written file.

started.description:
Apple's installer window was asked for. It runs on its own from there;
`GET /api/setup/tools` says when git is ready.

GitState.description: Whether git is there to use.

Injection.description:
State of a message remote-hand injected into a session.

Filled in by `crate::inject::InjectionRegistry`; `null` for a session
remote-hand has never driven.

InstallMethod.description: How a CLI was installed, read off where its binary really lives.

ItemKind.description: What kind of content an item carries.

Level.description:
How loudly a nudge arrives, under Bark's own names.

Bark has a fourth, `critical`, which bypasses silent mode and Do Not Disturb.
It is deliberately absent: a model deciding on its own that something is
worth waking a person at four in the morning is exactly the failure this
feature would be remembered for, and the user who really wants that can set
it on the Bark side per group.

LimitClass.description: What kind of limit a failure was.

LinkAttempt.description: An attempt: what the opener page hands the popup.

aggregator.description: The aggregator's pending keys (when aggregation was asked for).

handoffUrl.description:
The droppen.app address that answers this attempt through the browser
instead of the popup (§4.9: the desktop app's window, a blocked popup):
`<hub>/link#droppen-link=…`. It carries the attempt's state in its
fragment — never in a query, never logged. `null` when the request
said no `Origin` to come back to.

hubWeb.description:
The popup's origin, where the browser signs in: the hub's app origin
(`https://my.droppen.app`), else its own (`https://droppen.app`).

nonce.description:
The nonce the popup's messages must carry (32 hex digits). Only ever
between this page and the popup — never in a URL.

LinkEnrolled.description:
An already-enrolled computer's place, for the popup's "only add the
aggregator" variant.

accountFp.description: The account key's fingerprint, 32 hex digits.

id.description: The machine id.

LinkMachine.description: The machine's keys for the popup to check the enrollment proof against.

enrolled.description: Set when this computer is enrolled already.

aggregate.description: Also run this computer as an aggregator (default `true`).

LocalAccountAccess.description: A local account, and whether it may see the other devices here (S1-7).

owner.description:
Whether it is the owner (it signed this device in, or claimed it):
it always sees them, and decides who else does.

remote.description: Whether it sees the other devices here now.

LocalLogin.description: The machine's own login for one CLI.

isDefault.description:
Somebody made it this CLI's default (`PUT /api/accounts/default` with
`null`, the local-login radio in Settings). A start that names no account
then runs on it whatever its state: a choice, not the absence of one, so
nothing takes its place when it is signed out.

rest.description:
Its active rests, in the shape `Account.rest` uses — a refused credential
as much as a quota window it ran out of.

state.description: Whether it can start a session, as far as this server can tell.

LocalLoginState.description:
Whether the machine's own login can start a session right now, as far as
this server can tell.

LocalLogins.description: Both CLIs' local logins, as `AccountList.local` reports them.

token.description:
A one-time local-open token for this server's page
(`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#local-open=<token>`), good once within a
minute; `null` when the instance has a user account, whose login page
is the one to open.

The one-time token `remote-hand-server open` put in the page's address
(after `#local-open=`). In the body, never in a URL.

password.description:
The password, in the clear — this connection is expected to be loopback,
a tunnel, or TLS terminated in front of it.

LoginResult.description: What a successful login hands back.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working, ISO-8601. Absolute; using it does not extend it.

token.description:
The bearer token. **The only copy**: the server keeps a sha256 of it and
cannot reproduce this string, so a client that loses it logs in again.

LoginState.description: What the CLI's own status command says about its login.

MathStyle.description: How LaTeX math in a message renders.

at.description: When the status last changed, ISO-8601.

clientMessageId.description: The id the client sent the message under.

qid.description: The queue id it travels under, as `resident.queuedMessages[].id` names it.

ModelInfo.description: One model the local CLI can be asked for.

defaultEffort.description: The effort used when the caller picks none.

id.description: The id passed to the CLI.

label.description: Human-facing name, when the CLI publishes one.

models.description: Models currently known to the local CLI, freshest first.

source.description: Whether `models` came from the CLI's cache or from the static fallback.

ModelListSource.description:
Where a model list came from.

On the wire so the picker can say so. A list the CLI itself published — read
out of its cache, or asked of it directly — describes the models this
account may actually run; the fallback is a static guess that exists only so
the picker is never empty, and one shown as if it were the other is how a
user ends up picking a model their CLI does not have.

ModelUsage.description: One model's share of the window, on one CLI.

cacheRead.description: Tokens served from the prompt cache.

cacheWrite.description: Tokens written into the prompt cache.

cost.description: Estimated USD at published API rates, or null when the model is unpriced.

model.description: Model id as the transcript recorded it.

accountFrom.description:
`"start"`: `accountId` is the account `GET /api/accounts/start` named
for a pair no model-less start reaches (`placed: false`), not a pick —
logged as the start rule's choice and checked again at the spawn.

accountId.description: Run under a stored Claude account; `null` means the local login.

clientMessageId.description:
A UUID the client minted for this first message, sent unchanged with
every attempt. A repeat answers the session the first attempt started
(`duplicate: true`) instead of starting a second one.

cwd.description: Working directory for the new session.

files.description:
Non-image attachment paths returned by `POST /api/uploads`, sent with
the first message.

images.description:
Image paths returned by `POST /api/uploads`, sent with the first
message exactly as `POST /api/sessions/{source}/{id}/message` takes them.

NewSessionResult.description: The id of the session that was just created.

duplicate.description:
`true` when this answers a retry of an already-accepted
`clientMessageId`: no second session was started.

id.description: The CLI's own session id.

NotifyBody.description: The body of `POST /api/notify`, which is what `rh-notify` sends.

group.description: How the phone stacks these; the session's own title when absent.

level.description: How loudly it should arrive; `active` when absent.

title.description: The headline. Required, and the one thing the user reads first.

NotifyConfigInfo.description:
What a client is allowed to learn about the configuration.

The endpoint is not in it. Its last path segment is the Bark device key,
which is the entirety of Bark's authorization, so what comes back is a mask:
enough to recognise the endpoint you configured, and not enough to send to
it. Same rule as [`crate::chats::provider::ChatProviderInfo`]'s `hasKey`, one
step friendlier because there is only ever one of these and a user with two
phones should be able to tell which one is armed.

baseUrl.description:
How a phone reaches this server, for the link a notification carries.
Not a secret, and returned in full so the settings page can edit it.

enabled.description: Whether sessions may nudge at all.

endpointMask.description: The endpoint with its device key masked, or `""` when there is none.

NotifyConfigUpdate.description:
The body of `PUT /api/notify/config`; every field is a patch.

A patch rather than a whole document because the endpoint is write-only from
the client's side: a settings page that has never been shown the device key
cannot send it back, and a `PUT` of everything it *can* see would erase it.

baseUrl.description: A new base URL for notification links; an empty string drops the links.

enabled.description: Turn nudges on or off without forgetting the endpoint.

endpoint.description:
A new endpoint — a full URL or a bare Bark device key. An explicit empty
string forgets the stored one.

currentPassword.description:
The current password. Required even though the caller is authenticated:
a token left behind on an unlocked laptop must not be enough to take the
account over.

newPassword.description: The replacement, which has to satisfy the same rules `user add` applies.

PatchHunk.description:
One hunk of a unified diff, as the CLI records it on an edit's result.

The shape is Claude Code's own: the top-level `toolUseResult.structuredPatch`
of the entry carrying an `Edit`/`MultiEdit`/`Write` result. `lines` holds the
raw diff rows, each already prefixed with `-`, `+` or a space, so a renderer
can colour them without re-deriving the diff.

newLines.description: How many lines the hunk covers after the edit.

newStart.description: First line of the hunk in the file as it now is.

oldLines.description: How many lines the hunk covered before the edit.

oldStart.description: First line of the hunk in the file as it was.

PathRead.description: How the most recent read of the login shell went.

PluginBatch.description: The body of `POST /api/plugins/{id}/batch`: all of these, or none.

writes.description: In order; a name may appear once.

docs.description: Every document written, in the order of the writes.

PluginCurrentDoc.description:
The document a conflict names, as it is now.

The same JSON as [`PluginDoc`], under a name of its own: the `409` may
carry `null` here, and the OpenAPI pass that spells a nullable reference
marks the *component* nullable (`openapi_ext::hoist_nullable_refs`), which
would make every `PluginDoc` read as possibly `null`.

revision.description: Bumped by every write; the first write makes it 1.

value.description: The plugin's JSON; the host never interprets it.

PluginDocConflict.description: The `409`: which document moved, and what it is now.

current.description: That document as it is now; `null` when it does not exist.

doc.description: The first document whose revision did not hold.

more.description: Older versions remain; ask again with `offset` moved past these.

versions.description:
Newest first: `limit` of them (ten unless asked, at most fifty), fewer
when their values pass 8 MiB together (the first is always there).

PluginDocVersion.description: One past version of a document.

updatedBy.description: Who wrote it, when the host knows.

expectedRevision.description:
The revision the write is based on; `null` means "must not exist yet".
(Read leniently: a body without it means `null`, as the SDK's does.)

PluginNotice.description: One thing a plugin's host wants the user to see.

dismissible.description:
Whether a client may dismiss it. Kept for the wire contract; a store
reset goes away when the user clears its file.

id.description: Stable while the notice exists.

expectedRevision.description:
The revision the write is based on; `null` means "must not exist yet".
(Read leniently: a body without it means `null`, as the SDK's does.)

PluginStatus.description: A plugin as this instance sees it.

enabled.description: On for this instance, and compatible.

forced.description: The configuration pins it on or off; the switch is read-only.

notice.description:
A problem that does not stop it working: today, a store that had to be
reset. Every notice's text, joined.

reason.description: Why it is off, incompatible or pinned, when it is.

enabled.description: On or off, for this instance.

limit.description: The limit that was passed, in bytes.

path.description:
The practice folder, absolute and empty: the one made last if it still
is, else one just made.

diagrams.description: How a Mermaid diagram in a message renders; a body without it means `rendered`.

language.description: UI language; `auto` follows the browser locale.

math.description: How LaTeX math in a message renders; a body without it means `rendered`.

sessionGrouping.description: How the session list is grouped.

QuestionAnswerResult.description: What answering or dismissing a question did.

question.description: The question as it now stands.

QuestionEntry.description: A question the model is waiting on an answer for.

header.description: Short header shown above the options.

multiSelect.description: Whether more than one option may be picked.

description.description: Longer explanation, when the model supplied one.

QuestionState.description: Where a question is in its life.

QueuedMessage.description:
One message a resident has been given and has not answered yet.

The queue used to be a number, which is enough to say "something is waiting"
and not enough to do anything about it: a user who queued the wrong message
behind a half-hour turn could neither see what they had sent nor take it
back. Each entry carries the id the two queue routes take —
`DELETE /api/sessions/{source}/{id}/queue/{qid}` and
`POST /api/sessions/{source}/{id}/queue/{qid}/steer`.

id.description:
Stable for as long as the message waits, and across a restart: it is
written to the journal with the message. Never reused.

steered.description:
Whether this one has already been written to claude's stdin, ahead of
its turn, by a steer.

It is still counted in [`ResidentInfo::queued`] because it has not run
yet — but it is past the point of being taken back, so a client should
offer neither Delete nor Steer on it. Both answer `409`.

text.description:
The prompt, cut to a preview length with an ellipsis where it was cut.

A preview rather than the whole thing because this rides on every list
row: the transcript is where a prompt is read in full, and a queue of
hundred-thousand-character messages would otherwise be sent to a phone
once a second.

claude.description: The user's own login, or `null` when there is nothing to report.

QuotaProbeError.description:
Why an account has no windows.

`not_logged_in` is a verdict — the CLI ran and reported nothing — while
`probe_failed` only says the reading did not happen, so the UI must not send
the user back through `claude auth login` for it.

QuotaReadingSource.description: Where an account's quota reading came from: the rate-limit events of a live session, or the `/usage` probe the server falls back to when no session has run for a while.

QuotaWindow.description: One rolling window of a subscription.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 of when this window was read. Windows of one reading can differ in age.

usedPercent.description: How much of it is gone, 0–100.

windowMinutes.description: The window's length in minutes; 0 when unknown.

fingerprint.description: The new identity key's fingerprint (8 groups of 4 hex digits).

state.description: `unenrolled`: it waits for a registration code.

receipts.description: The ids this server accepted for this session.

unknown.description:
The ids this server never saw: nothing was enqueued under them, so the
message is safe to send again — under the same id.

ReceiptStatus.description: What became of a message, as far as this server knows.

RecentCwds.description: The directories recent sessions were started in.

cwds.description: Absolute paths, most recently started in first.

RecentFolder.description: A folder sessions ran in on this device.

lastUsed.description: The newest activity of a session there, ISO-8601.

path.description: Absolute, as the sessions recorded it.

folders.description: At most six, the most recently used first; only folders that still exist.

RemoteAccess.description: One local account's access to other machines.

remote.description: Whether it may see and use other machines.

patient.description: Give the login shell 20 s instead of 5 ("look again, slowly").

ResidentInfo.description:
What this server's resident CLI says about a session.

Present exactly when *this* server holds a live process for the session, and
absent for external sessions and legacy one-shot runs. A client that finds it here should prefer it to
every other signal on the row: it is the process' own account of itself,
not an inference from the file it writes.

asking.description:
Whether claude is blocked on an `AskUserQuestion` this server is holding
open, mid-turn, waiting for the user's answer.

The process' own word, so it is what [`apply_driver`] reports as the
row's `asking` — while the turn is `working`, which is exactly when a
question is open. Always false for codex. `#[serde(default)]` for rows a
cache wrote before the field existed.

awaitingBackground.description:
Whether the head of the queue is parked waiting for that background work.

A message asking for a different model, effort or account needs a new
process, and replacing the running one would kill whatever it is minding
in the background — so it waits. Without this the session reads as
simply idle with something queued, which is indistinguishable from a bug.

background.description:
How many background tasks claude is still minding.

These outlive the turn that started them, which is why a session can be
`idle` and still be doing work.

Stays the authoritative number. `tasks` is capped and this is not, so a
session minding more than the cap reports all of them here and describes
the first hundred there.

phase.description: Where the process is in its cycle.

queued.description:
How many messages are waiting behind whatever is in flight.

The field the composer was missing: a send that is answered
`{"accepted":true,"queued":true}` had nowhere to show up afterwards, so
a user who sent one while a turn was running saw a session that looked
finished and a message that had apparently vanished.

Counts the steered messages too: they have been handed to claude but
have not run, so a session with one of them outstanding is not finished.
Always equal to `queuedMessages.len()`.

queuedMessages.description:
The messages behind that count, in the order they will run.

Steered messages first — they are already in claude's stdin, so they run
before anything still waiting here — then the queue proper, oldest
first.

stalled.description:
Whether the turn in flight has produced nothing for a long time.

Never a reason to kill anything; it is the flag a Stop button is offered
beside.

tasks.description:
Those tasks, oldest first, as far as the CLI described them.

Empty whenever `background` is zero, and never longer than the cap the
driver publishes — see [`crate::inject::resident::TASKS_ON_THE_WIRE`].

turnStartedAt.description:
When the turn in flight began, by this server's clock, ISO-8601; `null`
between turns.

The moment the resident left `idle` for `starting` or `working`, so a
list row can say how long a session has been at it. Kept across a
recovery inside one turn, and cleared when the turn ends. Null for a
driver that does not track it (codex's app-server).

ResidentPhase.description:
Where a resident process is in its cycle.

The wire form of `crate::inject::resident::Phase`. A separate type because
the driver's is an internal enum that the injection subsystem is free to
grow states on, and this one is a contract.

ReturnRequest.description:
`POST /api/cloud/link/return`: droppen.app's sealed reply, as the page at
`/link/return` took it from its address.

cwd.description:
Working directory the session starts in, already resolved and checked to
be a directory when it was stored.

enabled.description: Whether the runner looks at it at all.

expr.description:
The five-field cron expression, read in the server's local time zone.
See [`cron`] for why that zone and not UTC.

id.description: Stable id, a uuid v4.

lastError.description: The detail behind a `failed` or `invalidExpression`, for a person to read.

lastRunAt.description:
When the scheduler last acted on it, ISO-8601 — which is not the same as
"last ran": a skip is an action and sets this too.

lastSessionId.description:
The session the last successful run started, and the one `skipIfBusy`
asks about.

model.description: `--model`, or `null` for the CLI's own default.

nextRunAt.description: When it next fires, ISO-8601, or `null` while it is disabled or unusable.

prompt.description: The first — and, for this feature, only — prompt.

skipIfBusy.description:
Skip this run when the session the last one made is still busy.

On by default. remote-hand's queue never refuses a message — it waits — so
without this a half-hourly task whose sessions take forty minutes would
quietly build a backlog that only ever grows.

ScheduledTaskCreate.description:
The body of `POST /api/scheduled-tasks`.

The four required fields are the ones a task cannot be invented without; the
rest are [`Optional`] rather than `Option` throughout, because the contract is
zod's `.optional()` and a plain `Option` would document `T | null`.

cwd.description: Working directory; must exist and be under the home directory.

enabled.description:
Whether it starts enabled. Defaults to `true`: a task nobody asked to be
dormant was created to run.

name.description: Display name; blank or missing becomes `task N`.

prompt.description: The prompt the session starts with.

skipIfBusy.description: Skip a run whose predecessor is still busy. Defaults to `true`.

ScheduledTaskUpdate.description:
The body of `PATCH /api/scheduled-tasks/{id}`; every field is a patch.

An empty string in `model`, `effort` or `permission` clears it back to the
CLI's own default — the one thing an absent field cannot express, and the
only way a user who set a model once can unset it.

cwd.description: New working directory; checked exactly as on create.

enabled.description:
Start or stop looking at it. Enabling reschedules from now, so a task
switched back on does not immediately fire for a time that has passed.

expr.description: New cron expression. Reschedules from now.

name.description: New display name; a blank one is ignored.

skipIfBusy.description: Whether to skip a run whose predecessor is still busy.

source.description:
Switch which CLI the run starts. The flags are re-checked against it, so
a `permission` the other CLI has never heard of is refused here rather
than at the spawn.

ScopeFilter.description:
Which scopes a listing asks for.

Separate from [`SessionScope`] because it has a third answer a row never has:
`all`, which is what the global feed and the directory picker want.

emoji.description: Custom rail icon; absent uses the default grid icon.

id.description: Stable id, a uuid v4.

layout.description:
The sanitized pane tree. Client-owned in shape, which is why the schema
says `any` and why the server rebuilds it rather than storing it.

revision.description:
Bumped by every successful write to this screen, starting at 1. A
`PATCH` names the revision it was based on and is refused with `409`
when the screen has moved on since.

ScreenConflict.description: The `409` a `PATCH` gets when the screen changed since its `baseRevision`.

screen.description: The screen as it is now, for the client to adopt.

baseListRevision.description:
The list revision the client last saw; when given and stale, nothing is
created and the answer is `409` with the current list.

title.description:
Display name; a missing or blank one becomes `screen N`.

[`Optional`] rather than `Option`: the contract is `z.string().optional()`
without `.nullable()`, and a plain `Option` documents `string | null`.

listRevision.description:
Bumped by every create, delete and reorder, starting at 1. A list
operation may name it as `baseListRevision` to be refused when stale.

ScreenListConflict.description: The `409` a list operation gets when its `baseListRevision` is stale.

screens.description: The list as it is now.

baseListRevision.description:
The list revision the client last saw; when given and stale, nothing
moves and the answer is `409` with the current list.

ids.description:
Screen ids in the order wanted. Ids the server does not have are
ignored, and screens the list does not name keep their relative order
after the ones it does — so a reorder from a device that has not seen a
screen another one just made cannot lose it.

baseRevision.description:
The revision this change was made against. It must still be the stored
one; otherwise nothing is written and the answer is `409` with the
screen as it is now.

emoji.description: One emoji; blank restores the default icon, absent leaves it alone.

layout.description:
New pane tree; absent leaves it alone.

The custom deserializer is what keeps "absent" and "`null`" apart:
[`Optional`] alone folds a JSON `null` into `None`, but the TypeScript
treats an explicit `null` as a layout that was *supplied* and sanitizes
it down to a single empty pane.

title.description: New display name; absent leaves it alone.

SearchField.description: Which part of an item a match's snippet was cut from.

SearchMatch.description: One item of the transcript that holds every term of the query.

field.description:
Which part of the item `snippet` was cut from: the one holding the most
distinct terms, `text` before `tool` before `detail` on a tie.

index.description:
Absolute index of the item, in the numbering of the session feed's
`startIndex`/`endIndex` and of `GET …/history`.

kind.description: What kind of content it carries.

ranges.description:
Every hit inside `snippet` as `[start, end)` offsets in UTF-16 code
units — so `snippet.slice(start, end)` in JavaScript is the hit — sorted
and with overlapping hits merged.

snippet.description:
At most 160 characters of that field around its first hit, whitespace
runs collapsed to one space, with `…` where it was cut.

timestamp.description: The item's own timestamp, when the transcript has one.

SeenResult.description: What marking a session read answers.

accepted.description: Always true; the shape every other accept-only route answers with.

previousReadAt.description:
The mark this one replaced: when the user had last looked before now,
ISO-8601, or `null` for a session never marked (or whose mark was
evicted).

The reader arriving at a session reports it seen at once, and that
report is what moves the mark — so this is the only reliable place to
learn where their unread messages began. A client hands it to
`GET /api/sessions/{source}/{id}/first-unread?after=` to offer the way
back to the first of them.

SelfUpgrade.description: The outcome of replacing the server binary.

detail.description: Why `restart` is what it is, in a sentence meant to be shown.

ok.description: Always true; a failure is an `Error` body with a 4xx or 5xx status.

previousVersion.description: The version of the server that answered this request.

restart.description:
`restarting` when a supervisor will bring the new binary up by itself,
`manual` when the swap is done but somebody has to restart the server.

version.description: The version the uploaded binary reports for itself.

accountId.description: Run under a stored Claude account; `null` means the local login.

clientMessageId.description:
A UUID the client minted when the message was created, sent unchanged
with every attempt. A repeat is answered with the first attempt's answer
(`duplicate: true`) and enqueues nothing; see `GET …/receipts`.

model.description: Model id, passed to the CLI as a flag value.

SendMessageResult.description:
The answer to a send, which now has one more thing to say than "done".

A separate type rather than a field on [`SendResult`] because the other
routes that answer with one — rename, archive, interrupt — have no queue and
never will, and a field that is always `false` for most of its users is a
worse contract than a second shape.

accepted.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

answered.description:
`true` when the agent was blocked on a question and the message went in
as its answer (the question's free-text `response`) rather than into the
queue behind the turn it would otherwise have waited for; `false` when a
question was open but could not take it — answered from another screen a
moment before, stopped, or the session still reconnecting — so it was
delivered as an ordinary message (`queued` says whether it waits).
Absent when no question was open.

duplicate.description:
`true` when this answers a retry: the `clientMessageId` was already
accepted, nothing was enqueued again, and this is what the first
attempt answered.

qid.description:
The queue id the message travels under (`resident.queuedMessages[].id`),
when the request carried a `clientMessageId`.

queued.description:
The message went in behind a turn that is still running, and will be
delivered when that turn ends. Only a resident claude answers `true`.

SendResult.description: The answer to every route that only has to say "done".

accepted.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error status, not a `false`.

ServerBinaryUpload.description:
The `multipart/form-data` body this route reads.

gotcha derives nothing from a `Multipart` extractor, so the parts the handler
looks at are documented by hand, exactly as the file uploads do.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of `binary`. Optional; verified when present.

accountId.description: The account this session runs under; `null` unbinds it.

SessionActivity.description:
Whether anything is in flight for a session, in one word.

[`SessionStatus`] is a *guess*: it comes from a live-process registration
plus a heuristic over the tail of the transcript, and both halves are wrong
in the cases that matter most — a turn whose recent writing is all
sidechain reads as `waiting`, and a message queued behind a turn is
invisible to it entirely. This is the answer the driver gives, and where
this server holds the process it is not a guess at all.

Deliberately one word rather than a set of flags. The question a list row
has to answer is "is this session doing something, and if not, why is my
message not moving" — four answers cover it, and the detail is on
[`ResidentInfo`] for whoever wants it.

SessionAgent.description:
One agent that wrote a transcript under a session, however it was spawned.

The index behind the drill-down. Every field but the id may be missing,
because the meta the CLI writes beside an agent may itself be missing or
half-filled — a Skill-spawned agent's meta is `{"agentType":…,"spawnDepth":1}`

SessionScope.description:
Whose session this is, from this server's point of view.

The distinction the whole list is built on. A server *owns* the sessions it
made: a claude transcript in the Claude root this instance owns, or a codex
thread whose id is in this instance's own record. Everything else — the
user's own `~/.claude`, another remote-hand's sessions, a codex thread started
from a terminal — is **external**: readable, searchable, openable, but not
this server's to drive.

Ownership is not a permission check; it is a statement about who is allowed to
*resume* a conversation. Two servers resuming one transcript interleave their
turns into it, which is the failure this replaces with a `409`.

tell a queued message from an idle session, and background work from
nothing at all.

asking.description:
Whether the agent has stopped to ask the user something, and cannot go
on without an answer.

Much narrower than `status: waiting`, which only says a live process
finished its turn — and this server keeps a finished session's process
alive, so that is true of nearly every session it drives. For a session
this server drives it is the resident's own word ([`ResidentInfo::asking`]):
true from the moment claude's `AskUserQuestion` arrives until it is
answered, dismissed or withdrawn — mid-turn, so while `activity` says
`working`. For any other live claude it is read off the transcript: a
tail ending on an `AskUserQuestion` no result has answered yet, and never
while [`apply_driver`] knows a turn is in flight. Always false for codex:
it runs with approvals off, and every interactive request its app server
makes is refused, so it has no way to stop and ask.

`#[serde(default)]` for the summaries [`crate::db::index`] cached before
this field existed; the live overlay fills it in.

file's mtime for a transcript too odd to date. Appending to a session
moves `updatedAt` and never this, which is what lets recent directories
be ranked by where work was started rather than by what is loudest.

Every worktree of one repository shares this, so a client can group the
four checkouts of one project into one heading instead of four. Purely a
display key: it never widens what a server lists, and two sessions sharing
a `repoKey` have no relationship beyond the repository they sit in.

resident.description:
This server's resident process for the session, when it has one.

Null for every session this server does not drive, which is most of
them: an external transcript, a codex thread, a claude somebody's own
terminal has open.

[`Nullable`] rather than a bare `Option` because the field is always
*present* on the wire and is `null` when there is no resident, which is
what a client reading it as `row.resident?.phase` needs the schema to
say.

server.description:
Which remote-hand server this row came from, as [`ServerId`] spells it.

It answers two subtly different questions depending on `scope`, and the
difference is worth stating because a client will eventually route on
this:

* **`owned`** — the server that *made* the session. Read from the
session's own ownership row ([`owned_sessions`]), so it survives a
restart and is a claim about history.
* **`external`** — the server the session is *reachable through*. A
discovered transcript (the user's own `~/.claude`, a codex thread
started from a terminal) was made by nobody here; what is true of it
is that this server can see the file and serve its contents, so this
server names itself.

Both answers are "the server to ask about this row", which is what makes
one field reasonable; neither is "the machine the work happened on", and
nothing should read it as that.

Filled in by the ownership overlay — `claude::mark_owned` and
`codex::apply_ownership` — alongside `scope`, because both can change
without the transcript being touched and neither may be cached against
it. `#[serde(default)]` for the summaries [`crate::db::index`] cached
before this field existed: they parse, and the overlay fills them in.

post.description:
Ask claude to stop one background task, leaving the turn in flight alone.

Separate from [`interrupt_session`] because they are separate verbs. Stop
ends the turn and leaves every background task running; this ends one task
and leaves the turn — and the other tasks — running. Neither substitutes for
the other, and the panel draws them in different places for that reason.

CLI reports that by publishing its task list again without the task in it,
which reaches the client over the session stream it is already reading — so
the row disappearing is the confirmation, and a row that stays is a stop that
did not take.
